title: Get Started
text: reveal_aes() splits plot levels aesthetic mapping. , sex mapped color, reveal_aes(p1, aes = "color") produces list three plots: first blank layout, plot adding male penguins, finally one adds female penguins.  default, first plot list blank frame showing layout elements (axes, legend, facet labels, etc) data, last plot identical original plot. See section Controlling reveal order modify behaviour. reveal_aes() accepts aesthetic. Mapping sex shape instead:  Note even though geom_smooth() use shape aesthetic, reveal_aes() also groups lines sex shape defined global call aes(). shape defined inside geom_point(), regression lines appear together single step. reveal_x() reveal_y() shortcuts reveal_aes(aes = "x") reveal_aes(aes = "y"). work best axis variable discrete values:  find needing incrementally reveal large number values (e.g. time series developing x axis), might want use gganimate instead. reveal_groups() equivalent reveal_aes(aes = "group"). useful groups implicit (ggplot2 automatically groups data interaction discrete variables).
code: reveal_aes(p1, aes = "color") p2 <- ggplot(penguins,              aes(x = body_mass_g,                  y = bill_length_mm,                  shape = sex)) +       geom_point() +       geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = "y ~ x", linewidth = 1) +       facet_wrap(~species) +       scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 15)) +       theme_minimal()  reveal_aes(p2, aes = "shape") p3 <- ggplot(penguins,              aes(x = sex, y = bill_length_mm)) +       geom_boxplot() +       theme_minimal()  reveal_aes(p3, aes = "x")

title: Get Started
text: reveal_patchwork() works composite figures built patchwork package, revealing one constituent plot time. first element list shows overall patchwork layout child plots blanked . subsequent element adds one child plot, order composed. final element matches original patchwork.
code: library(patchwork)  p4 <- ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species)) +       geom_bar() +       theme_minimal()  pw <- p1 / (p3 + p4)  reveal_patchwork(pw)

title: Get Started
text: main reveal_* functions accept order argument: numeric vector specifies elements reveal sequence. lets : Reorder sequence. example, reveal species reverse order reveal_panels():  Skip elements. Omit step entirely leaving index :  Drop blank opening frame including -1 order vector:  order argument works identically across reveal_aes(), reveal_groups(), reveal_layers(), reveal_panels(), reveal_patchwork().
code: # Default: Adelie → Chinstrap → Gentoo # Reversed: Gentoo → Chinstrap → Adelie reveal_panels(p1, order = c(3, 2, 1)) # Only reveal Adelie (panel 1) and Gentoo (panel 3), skipping Chinstrap reveal_panels(p1, order = c(1, 3)) # Start directly with data, no blank frame reveal_panels(p1, order = c(-1, 1, 2, 3))

title: Get Started
text: reveal_save() saves plot list numbered file using ggsave(). extra arguments (e.g. width, height) forwarded directly ggsave(): produces files like myplot_0.png, myplot_1.png, myplot_2_last.png.
code: reveal_save(plot_list, "myplot.png", width = 9, height = 5)

title: Get Started
text: manipulate basic components ggplot object (layers, geoms, facets), functions ggreveal work ggplot2 extensions.1 examples:
code: library(ggridges)  p_ridges <- ggplot(penguins,                    aes(x = bill_length_mm,                        y = species,                        fill = sex)) +             geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.6) +             theme_minimal()  reveal_y(p_ridges) # Adapted from ggpubr docs library(ggpubr) data("ToothGrowth") my_comparisons <- list( c("0.5", "1"), c("1", "2"), c("0.5", "2") )  p_ggpubr <- ggviolin(ToothGrowth, x = "dose", y = "len", fill = "dose",                     palette = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"),                    add = "boxplot", add.params = list(fill = "white")) +             stat_compare_means(comparisons = my_comparisons, label = "p.signif")  reveal_layers(p_ggpubr) library(geobr) library(sf) library(ggmapinset)  states <- read_state() campos <- read_municipality(code_muni=3301009) rj <- read_municipality(code_muni=3304557)  inset1 <- configure_inset(   shape_circle(     centre =  st_centroid(campos),     radius = 70   ),   scale = 4,   translation = c(450, 0) )  inset2 <- configure_inset(   shape_circle(     centre =  st_centroid(rj),     radius = 70   ),   scale = 4,   translation = c(0, -450) )  p_br <- ggplot() +       geom_sf(data = states,                group = 1) +        geom_sf_inset(data = campos,                      inset = inset1,                     fill = "#00BFC4",                     group = 2) +       geom_inset_frame(inset = inset1,                         group = 2) +              geom_sf_inset(data = rj,                      inset = inset2,                     fill = "#00BFC4",                     group = 3) +       geom_inset_frame(inset = inset2,                        group = 3) +       theme_minimal()   reveal_aes(p_br, "group")

title: Reveal a ggplot Incrementally
text: Create graph ggplot2 usual.  use one reveal_* functions (reveal_layers(), reveal_aes(), reveal_groups(), reveal_panels(), reveal_x()) obtain list plots show elements incrementally.    can also use reveal_patchwork() incrementally reveal individual plots patchwork object. common use case show plots different slides presentation. can work directly list plots returned functions (useful Quarto R Markdown presentations), save plots separate files include presentation software choice. reveal_save() convenient function save plots list:
code: library(palmerpenguins) library(ggplot2) library(ggreveal)  p <-  ggplot(penguins[!is.na(penguins$sex),],              aes(body_mass_g, bill_length_mm,                  group=sex, color=sex)) +       geom_point() +       geom_smooth(method="lm", formula = 'y ~ x', linewidth=1) +       facet_wrap(~species) +       theme_minimal() p plot_list <- reveal_groups(p) plot_list #> [[1]] #>  #> [[2]] #>  #> [[3]] reveal_save(plot_list, "myplot.png", width = 8, height = 4) ── Saving incremental plots ──  ✔ myplot_0.png ✔ myplot_1.png ✔ myplot_2_last.png

title: Reveal plot by aesthetic — reveal_aes
text: Turns ggplot list plots, showing data incrementally arbitrary aesthetic.

title: Reveal plot by aesthetic — reveal_aes
code: reveal_aes(p, aes = "group", order = NULL, max = 20)

title: Reveal plot by aesthetic — reveal_aes
text: p ggplot2 object aes aesthetic reveal E.g.: group, colour, shape, linetype order (optional) numeric vector specifying order reveal levels specified aesthetic. example, aes='shape' plot uses three shapes, order = c(3, 2, 1) invert order revealed. shape included vector omitted incremental plots. E.g.: order = c(3, 1), second shape shown. default, first plot blank, showing layout elements (title, legends, axes, etc) data. omit blank plot, include -1: e.g. order = c(-1, 3, 1), order = -1. max maximum number unique levels aesthetic used

title: Reveal plot by aesthetic — reveal_aes
text: list ggplot2 objects, can passed reveal_save()

title: Reveal plot by aesthetic — reveal_aes
code: # Create full plot library(ggplot2)   p <- ggplot(mtcars,            aes(mpg, wt,               color = factor(vs),               group = factor(vs))) +    geom_point(aes(shape=factor(am)), size=2) +    geom_smooth(method="lm",                formula = 'y ~ x',                linewidth=1)   p    plot_list <- reveal_aes(p, "shape")  plot_list[[1]]   plot_list[[2]]   plot_list[[3]]   plot_list[[4]]    # Save plots reveal_save(plot_list, "myplot.png", width = 8, height = 4, path = tempdir()) #>  #> ── Saving incremental plots ── #>  #> ✔ /tmp/RtmpIa3asK/myplot_0.png #> ✔ /tmp/RtmpIa3asK/myplot_1.png #> ✔ /tmp/RtmpIa3asK/myplot_2.png #> ✔ /tmp/RtmpIa3asK/myplot_3_last.png  # Clean temp files file.remove(list.files(path = tempdir(), pattern = "myplot", full.names = TRUE))  #> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE

what: Reveal faceted plot by panel — reveal_panels
title: Reveal faceted plot by panel — reveal_panels
text: Turns ggplot list plots, showing data incrementally panels.

title: Reveal faceted plot by panel — reveal_panels
code: reveal_panels(p, order = NULL, what = c("data", "everything"))

title: Reveal faceted plot by panel — reveal_panels
text: p ggplot2 object order (optional) numeric vector specifying order reveal panels example, three panels plot, order = c(3, 2, 1) invert order revealed. panel included vector omitted incremental plots. E.g.: order = c(3, 1), second panel shown. default, first plot blank, showing layout elements (title, legends, axes, etc) data. omit blank plot, include -1: e.g. order = c(-1, 3, 1), order = -1. (optional) one "data" "everything".' "data" (default), basic graph layout, including axes facet labels, shown start, data points shown incrementally. "everything", entire panels shown incrementally.

title: Reveal faceted plot by panel — reveal_panels
text: list ggplot2 objects, can passed reveal_save()

title: Reveal faceted plot by panel — reveal_panels
code: # Create full plot library(ggplot2) data("mtcars")  p <- ggplot(mtcars,           aes(mpg, wt,              color = factor(vs),              group = factor(vs))) +   geom_point() +   geom_smooth(method="lm",               formula = 'y ~ x',               linewidth=1) +   facet_wrap(~am) p   # Only data plot_list <- reveal_panels(p, what = "data") plot_list[[1]]  plot_list[[2]]  plot_list[[3]]   # Everything plot_list <- reveal_panels(p, what = "everything") plot_list[[1]]  plot_list[[2]]  plot_list[[3]]   # Save plots reveal_save(plot_list, "myplot.png", width = 8, height = 4, path = tempdir()) #>  #> ── Saving incremental plots ── #>  #> ✔ /tmp/RtmpIa3asK/myplot_0.png #> ✔ /tmp/RtmpIa3asK/myplot_1.png #> ✔ /tmp/RtmpIa3asK/myplot_2_last.png  # Clean temp files file.remove(list.files(path = tempdir(), pattern = "myplot", full.names = TRUE))  #> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE

text: Turns patchwork list plots reveal child plot incrementally. Also works nesting insets.

title: Reveal plots from a patchwork object — reveal_patchwork
code: reveal_patchwork(pw, order = NULL)

title: Reveal plots from a patchwork object — reveal_patchwork
text: pw patchwork object order (optional) numeric vector specifying order reveal plots example, three plots patchwork, order = c(3, 2, 1) invert order revealed. plot included vector omitted incremental plots. E.g.: order = c(3, 1), second plot shown. default, first plot returned function blank, showing layout elements patchwork none child plots. omit blank plot, include -1: e.g. order = c(-1, 3, 1), order = -1.

title: Reveal plots from a patchwork object — reveal_patchwork
text: list ggplot2 objects

title: Reveal plots from a patchwork object — reveal_patchwork
code: library(ggplot2) library(patchwork) data("mtcars") p1 <- ggplot(mtcars,          aes(cyl,             fill = factor(am))) +       geom_bar()  +       labs(title = "Plot 1")  p2 <- ggplot(mtcars,          aes(disp,             fill = factor(am))) +       geom_histogram()  +       labs(title = "Plot 2")  p3 <- ggplot(mtcars,          aes(mpg, wt,             color = factor(vs))) +       geom_point() +       guides(color="none") +       labs(title = "Plot 3")  p4<- p3 +        coord_polar() +       theme_minimal() +       theme(axis.title = element_blank()) +       labs(title = "Plot 4")   pw <- (p1 + p2)/(p3 + inset_element(p4, 0.4, 0.4, 1.4, 1 )) +          plot_layout(guides = "collect")  plot_list <- reveal_patchwork(pw) #> `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`. plot_list[[1]]  plot_list[[2]]  plot_list[[3]]  plot_list[[4]]  plot_list[[5]]
